text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Government ready to ease limits on pension funds' investment in stocks, but more control must be exercised by workers and employers.
- Working group proposed a 150,000 markka limit on state guarantees of bank deposits, but customers can spread their risks by opening accounts in several banks. @
- Emeritus professor Viljo Rasila published the first Russian-language Finnish history book in 90 years.
- Disagreement brewing between copyright overseer Kopiosto and Real Estate Federation over payments of satellite broadcast rights.
- East Timorese Nobel peace prize laureate Jose Ramos-Horta on visit to Finland, calls on Finnish government to halt arms sales to Indonesia.
- High court suspended the license of a foreign-born medical practitioner, saying lacked language and professional skills. @
KAUPPALEHTI
- Taxation of small firms will increase in the next few years when temporary tax relief schemes end.
- SITRA fund matches private investor "business angels" with companies that need financing.
- National Board of Navigation to invite tenders for new ice-breaker. Troubled Finnyards must compete for the order alongside other shipbuilders.
- Consulting business put Arthur Andersen at top of Finnish accounting market with 30 percent share of net sales. @
AAMULEHTI
- More than 90 percent of Finns trust the police, study shows.
- Finnish champion wilderness trekker says it is impossible to get lost in Finland, if one can simply walk straight.
- Baby boom in Finnish parliament -- five MPs are pregnant.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Police say home-growth of marijuana on the rise in Finland -- even in Turku region.
- Economics professor Urpo Kivikari says economic laws no longer valid in Russia. @
